blocks.prompt: 5. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\sqrt{x}\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{y + \sqrt{x}}\).
blocks.explanation:
Right side \(e^{y + \sqrt{x}}\) mein power par jama hai, aur exponential jama ko zarb mein badal deta hai: \(e^{y + \sqrt{x}} = e^y e^{\sqrt{x}}\).
\(\sqrt{x}\) se divide karein to right side (sirf \(x\)) \(\times\) (sirf \(y\)) ban jati hai, yani separable.
Find kya karna hai? General solution.
Plan: \(e^{-y}\,dy = \frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\) banayenge; right wala integral \(u = \sqrt{x}\) se hal hoga.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sqrt{x}\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{y + \sqrt{x}}\), \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: general solution.
Tareeqa: Exponential ko torenge, variables alag karenge, aur dono taraf integrate karenge. Right side ke integral mein \(\sqrt{x}\) ki derivative mojood hai, is liye \(u = \sqrt{x}\) substitution kaam karegi.

Torein aur alag karein
\[\sqrt{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^y \cdot e^{\sqrt{x}}\]
\[e^{-y}\,dy = \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(e^{a + b} = e^a e^b\). Phir dono taraf \(e^y\) aur \(\sqrt{x}\) se divide kiya aur \(dx\) se multiply kiya; \(\frac{1}{e^y} = e^{-y}\).

Left side ka integral
\[\int e^{-y}\,dy = -e^{-y}\]
Kyun: \(e^{-y}\) ki derivative \(-e^{-y}\) hai (andar wale \(-y\) ki derivative \(-1\)). Is liye integral mein minus aata hai.
Dhyan dein: Yeh minus bhoolna is sawal ki sab se aam ghalti hai.

Right side ka integral (\(u = \sqrt{x}\))
\[du = \dfrac{dx}{2\sqrt{x}}, \quad \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,du\]
\[\int\dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx = 2\int e^u\,du\]
\[= 2e^{\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x}\) ki derivative \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) integral mein (2 ke farq ke saath) mojood hai. \(u\) rakhne se integral seedha \(2\int e^u\,du\) ban gaya.

Dono ko jorein
\[-e^{-y} = 2e^{\sqrt{x}} + c\]
\[e^{-y} + 2e^{\sqrt{x}} + C = 0\]
Kyun: \(-e^{-y}\) ko right par le gaye aur sab kuch ek taraf kar diya; \(C = c\) bhi arbitrary constant hi hai. Kitab ka jawab isi shakal mein hai.

Tasdeeq
\(e^{-y} + 2e^{\sqrt{x}} + C = 0\) ko differentiate karein:
\[-e^{-y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}} = 0\]
\[\sqrt{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^y e^{\sqrt{x}} = e^{y + \sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \(2e^{\sqrt{x}}\) ki derivative \(2e^{\sqrt{x}} \cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\). Dono taraf \(\sqrt{x}\,e^{y}\) se multiply karne par asal equation mil gayi.
